question: What is the main goal of a long term inflow and infiltration (I&I) strategy for a wastewater collection system?
correctAnswer: To reduce extraneous water entering the sewers so capacity is preserved for sanitary flow
explanation: I&I is groundwater and stormwater that should not be in the sanitary system. Reducing it preserves pipe and plant capacity, lowers overflow risk, and avoids treating clean water.
options: To increase the total flow reaching the treatment plant
To reduce extraneous water entering the sewers so capacity is preserved for sanitary flow
To replace every sewer main on a fixed ten year cycle
To eliminate the need for flow monitoring
optionA: To increase the total flow reaching the treatment plant
optionB: To reduce extraneous water entering the sewers so capacity is preserved for sanitary flow
optionC: To replace every sewer main on a fixed ten year cycle
optionD: To eliminate the need for flow monitoring
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Long Term I&I Strategy. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Long Term I&I Strategy

question: In collection system terminology, what does the abbreviation I&I stand for?
correctAnswer: Inflow and infiltration
explanation: I&I stands for inflow and infiltration: stormwater entering through direct connections and groundwater entering through defects in pipes, joints, and manholes.
options: Inspection and inventory
Internal inspection
Inflow and infiltration
Influent and intake
optionA: Inspection and inventory
optionB: Internal inspection
optionC: Inflow and infiltration
optionD: Influent and intake

question: A utility can fund I&I work in only three of its twelve sewersheds this year. How should a long term strategy rank the three?
correctAnswer: By measured wet weather flow response and overflow risk, starting with the worst performing basins
explanation: A data driven strategy ranks basins by measured rainfall dependent I&I, surcharge and overflow history, and consequence, so limited funds go where the flow reduction and risk reduction are greatest.
options: By measured wet weather flow response and overflow risk, starting with the worst performing basins
By the age of the neighbourhood alone
By which councillor asked most recently
Alphabetically by street name
optionA: By measured wet weather flow response and overflow risk, starting with the worst performing basins

optionC: By which councillor asked most recently
optionD: Alphabetically by street name

explanation: Effectiveness is verified by flow monitoring. Comparing wet weather response before and after rehabilitation, for comparable rainfall, shows whether extraneous flow actually fell.

Checking that the contractor invoices were paid
Asking residents whether the street looks better
Comparing post rehabilitation wet weather flow monitoring with the pre rehabilitation baseline for similar storms

optionB: Checking that the contractor invoices were paid

question: Flow studies show roughly half of a basin's I&I comes from private property sources such as laterals and foundation drains. What should the long term strategy include?
correctAnswer: A private side source removal component, such as lateral programs and downspout disconnection, where it is cost effective
explanation: When private sources contribute a large share of I&I, mainline work alone cannot deliver the target reduction. Cost effective private side programs are a standard part of a complete strategy.
options: Mainline lining only, since private sources are out of scope
A private side source removal component, such as lateral programs and downspout disconnection, where it is cost effective
Doubling the size of the trunk sewer instead of any source work
Waiting until every main has failed before acting
optionA: Mainline lining only, since private sources are out of scope
optionB: A private side source removal component, such as lateral programs and downspout disconnection, where it is cost effective
optionC: Doubling the size of the trunk sewer instead of any source work
optionD: Waiting until every main has failed before acting
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

correctAnswer: More intense rainfall events, flooding, freeze and thaw stress, and other changing weather extremes
explanation: Resilience planning addresses changing extremes, especially heavier rainfall that raises I&I and overflow risk, plus flooding of stations and freeze and thaw damage.

A change in the colour of sewer pipe
optionA: A permanent end to all rainfall
optionB: Lower water use in every home
optionC: More intense rainfall events, flooding, freeze and thaw stress, and other changing weather extremes

question: Residents repeatedly report sewer odours near one manhole, and a first inspection found nothing. What communication and follow up best serves the residents?
correctAnswer: Log the reports, investigate further at the times odours are reported, and report the findings and actions back to the residents

Tell residents the odour must come from somewhere else

Ask residents to stop calling about it

question: A utility must explain a sewer rate increase driven by aging infrastructure. Which message is most credible to the public?

A promise that this is the last increase ever

question: A utility inspects 4 percent of its sewers by CCTV each year while peer utilities inspect about 10 percent. What is the most useful conclusion from this benchmark?
correctAnswer: At the current rate a full inspection cycle takes about 25 years, so condition data will be too old to plan renewal well, and the gap deserves a management decision
explanation: Benchmarking turns a percentage into a planning consequence: a 25 year cycle means most condition information is badly dated, which weakens renewal decisions and justifies revisiting the rate.

CCTV results do not affect renewal planning

question: Before benchmarking its wet weather overflow rate against a peer utility, what must a manager check to keep the comparison honest?

question: Benchmarking shows a utility's cost per kilometre of sewer cleaned is well above peers, while its repeat blockage rate is also higher. What is the best management response?
correctAnswer: Investigate how the work is done, such as methods, equipment, and cleaning quality, and set an improvement target with follow up measurement
explanation: Paying more and getting worse results points to a method problem, not an effort problem. The response is to study the process, improve it, set a target, and verify with later measurement.

Order crews to clean faster with no other change
Stop reporting the cost figure
Cut the cleaning budget by the size of the gap

question: Why do strong programs track leading indicators, such as percentage of planned cleaning completed, alongside lagging indicators such as overflow counts?
correctAnswer: Leading indicators show whether the preventive work that drives future results is actually happening, before failures occur
explanation: Lagging indicators report harm after it happens. Leading indicators track the preventive activity that produces future performance, so managers can act before overflows rise.
options: Leading indicators are easier to make look good
Lagging indicators are not allowed in reports
Overflow counts are not real performance measures
Leading indicators show whether the preventive work that drives future results is actually happening, before failures occur
optionA: Leading indicators are easier to make look good
optionB: Lagging indicators are not allowed in reports
optionC: Overflow counts are not real performance measures
